summary: Adversarial verification of the closing-2 Lisvel art review. The machine load was 178 (1-minute average) during the check, so I made no timing or harness captures. I checked the cited artifacts directly; pixels, counts and FK numbers are valid at any load. All three majors are confirmed and there is no blocker. I re-score Lisvel at 7.0, not 7.5, so she is NOT ON PAR (the bar is 7.5). At the game camera the model and motion are close to the bar: the match75 x3 crop reads cleanly as a pale wrap, blue-grey tabard and diagonal bow, the visor now reads as glass, and the plate's nose and smile read as human. Cloth bones and the dash landing are real gains since the first closing review, which scored 6. But both the base and the Gorgewalk splash are clearly model renders on a painted plate. In the Gorgewalk card the bow limb crosses the head, so no face shows: the card shows a white, featureless, washed-out cut-out. The paid skin's body is the base's. Against a LoL skin and splash as the gauge, three open majors that sit on the skin and card surfaces do not fit a 7.5. Added findings: the dash starts at the apex with no takeoff, and in the base splash the bow hand grips the upper limb rather than the grip. Sensitivity: no blocker. The wrap is a rounded crown, the Wicks in frame show no eyes or mouth, and the base and Almanac faces show. Watch item: the Gorgewalk card's all-white, faceless figure is the closest thing on Lisvel to the blank-mannequin rule. M1's fix also clears it.

findings.title: Gorgewalk splash: the bow limb crosses the head, so no face shows, and the figure is a washed-out white cut-out
findings.what: Confirmed. In the 3x head crop the limb crosses the head at visor-to-mouth height. Above it are the wrap and the visor band; below it is a white chin and cowl with no features. The whole figure is near-white with a light fringe, in a side-on T-draw at the right edge (bbox width 0.125 of the frame). The reviewer says the face is 'hidden'. In practice the head reads as a featureless white wrapped form, which edges toward the blank-mannequin sensitivity rule. It is not a blocker, because no blank face plane is shown, only cloth, visor and bow.
findings.evidence: art/out/fighters/lisvel/lisvel_gorgewalk_splash.png; my crop _harness/_shots/closing_lisvel_v_gorge_head_x3.png (sips crop 240x260 at 1080,100, x3); _harness/_reports/closing_lisvel_r2_splash_stats.txt (torso luma 149 vs plate 87, figure width 0.125).
findings.gauge: A LoL skin splash is a painted composition: the face is legible, the figure owns the value range and is rim-separated, and the pose tells the skin's theme.
findings.fix:
As the review proposes, re-stage in lisvel.py CARDS (gorgewalk):
- Pose: the braced dash-landing crouch.
- Bow: held low, clear of the head.
- Camera: 3/4 from below.
- Grade: bring the figure's mid-tones into the plate's range, and leave a cool rim as the only near-white.
- Edge: erode the matte by 1 px.
- Gate: the face must read at portrait size.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced from the shipped PNG (Nov 4 23:36, current). The severity stands. Flagged as a sensitivity watch item (faceless white figure).

findings.title: Base splash: the string crosses the face, the top limb is cropped, the bow hand is on the upper limb, and the figure does not separate from the plate
findings.what: Confirmed on splash.png. The string runs from the cropped top tip (x about 970, y 0) through the cheek and mouth to the lower tip. The upper limb leaves the frame. A new detail: the bow hand grips at about y 180-260 on a bow that spans y 0-780, so the grip sits on the upper limb, not at the riser, which is an anatomically wrong hold. The figure torso (luma 92) is darker than the plate (101) and has no rim.
findings.gauge: A LoL base splash keeps the face clear of props, holds the weapon's full silhouette in frame, and separates the champion by value and rim light.
findings.fix: Follow the review's fix (a yaw of about 15 degrees, the tab hand at the jaw, pull back so both caps are in frame, a cool rim, a vignette behind the torso). Also put the bow hand on the riser at the bow's mid-length.
findings.files: art/blender/fighters/lisvel.py (CARDS base, splash light rig); art/out/fighters/lisvel/splash.png
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced. I added the off-centre grip.

findings.title: Gorgewalk's body is the base body; only the bow and quiver change
findings.what: Confirmed. In the close-up rows of the two sheets (front, back, side, face, shoulders, legs, belt) the tabard blue-grey, the chalk wrap and cowl, the leggings and the boots are the same. Gorgewalk differs only in a slate bow with rope bindings and a dark quiver. At the top-down rows the two skins cannot be told apart except by the bow tone.
findings.evidence: art/renders/fighters/lisvel/three_lisvel_gorgewalk.png vs three_lisvel.png (both Nov 6 08:43, current); the earlier CW5_r3_verify1 dE is 9.6 vs Almanac 16.1.
findings.gauge: A LoL skin is identifiable across the screen by the body's palette and material story, not by the weapon alone.
findings.fix:
As the review proposes, give Gorgewalk its own PAINT_SKIN:
- Wrap: a darker slate-sand, rope-bound.
- Tabard: lichen and damp-hem paint.
- Belt: cord-lashed.
- Gate: per-pixel dE of 16 or more vs base at the game camera.
- Keep the silhouette (ruling 7).

findings.title: Auto-attacks whip the bow about 1.9 m in the first two frames
findings.what: The bow tip moves 109 then 80 cm/frame in attack1, and 123 then 92 in attack2, with no anticipation.
findings.gauge: LoL marksman attacks show a short raise and draw read.
findings.fix: Ease the raise over f0-f3, with peak tip speed at most 40 cm/frame and the release time unchanged.

findings.title: Channel clip starts 172 cm off idle and then is frozen
findings.what: Every frame's tip step is 0; the hips range 0.0 cm and the chest 1.4 degrees. Channel is mapped in content/fighters/lisvel.json:524.
findings.gauge: LoL channels carry breath and held tension.
findings.fix: Add hip sway, chest breath and a string-tension pulse, and lead in from the guard.

findings.title: Portraits lose the bow, and Gorgewalk's portrait repeats the base pose
findings.gauge: A LoL portrait crop carries the signature prop along with the face.
findings.fix: Re-crop so the upper limb and its glass cap show behind the shoulder, and give Gorgewalk its own head angle.

findings.title: Pale shards under the lower belt; mottled sheen on the leggings
findings.gauge: LoL close-ups have clean part joins and controlled cloth specular.
findings.fix: Offset the skirt top 4 mm, and give the leggings a single matte roughness.

findings.title: Idle has little life
findings.what: Over the 3 s idle the hips move 1.6 cm and the chest 2.6 degrees, with no fidget.
findings.gauge: LoL idles carry a breath, a weight shift and a fidget.
findings.fix: Add a 3-4 cm weight shift, 5 degrees of breath and one fidget per loop.

findings.title: Dash starts at the apex with no takeoff (new)
findings.what: Dash f0 has the hips at 1.22 m against idle 0.94 (the bow tip is 43 cm from idle at f0), and the clip holds 1.22-1.20 for 7 frames before the landing. The jump-up is left to the crossfade, so Backstep pops into the air. The landing the review praises is real.
findings.gauge: LoL dashes show a readable push-off before the travel.
findings.fix: Key f0-f2 from the idle hip height through a crouch-push to the apex, and shorten the apex hold to 2-3 frames.
findings.verifierNote: Found in the reviewer's own FK report.
